clue.text: Girl gets May put back in calendar

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: put back tells us to turn the word for May round, end to start

parts.note: may, as in being permitted, means can

explanation.surface: A girl wangles her May holiday being moved later in the diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' reads as the month but is the verb meaning 'is allowed to'; 'put back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication built around a calendar of dates and events.

clue.text: Drug appears to help suppressing cold

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: aid means help
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drug seems to help by holding back a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the drug LSD.

clue.text: Doctor dancing samba in African port

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters of the following word moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor dances the samba in an African port.
explanation.definitionFit: Mombasa is the main seaport of Kenya in East Africa.

clue.text: Dark — almost totally, to start with

parts.note: nigh means almost

indicators.note: to start with means take only the opening letter of the word totally

explanation.surface: It is almost completely dark at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, so 'dark' as a noun names it.

clue.text: Chief pilot, the man in charge

parts.note: an airman is a pilot

explanation.surface: The chief pilot is the one who's in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman is the person who presides over a meeting or board.

clue.text: Disappointment was somehow deflating

explanation.surface: A disappointing result somehow took the wind out of someone's sails.
explanation.walkthrough: To let down a tyre is to deflate it; 'was somehow deflating' loosely describes that past action, with 'somehow' admitting the looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax or disappointment; letting down air from a tyre deflates it.

clue.text: Fire, or impose no punishment at all?

explanation.surface: Asks whether firing someone is no punishment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: To let off a gun is to fire it; a let-off is escaping punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting off a firework or gun discharges it; a let-off is being excused a penalty.

clue.text: Council official, one trying to restore confidence, loses heart after a short time

indicators.note: after places the shortened word behind the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: loses heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a reassurer tries to restore someone's confidence

explanation.surface: A local official who tries to calm people becomes dispirited before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' takes the middle S from REASSURER, leaving REASURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after the funds of a council or society, an officer of the body.

clue.text: Right ahead of the ball

explanation.surface: Correct to be in front of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the offside of a vehicle is its right-hand side; in football a player ahead of the ball may be offside.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage calls the right side of a car the offside; sports use it for illegally forward play.

clue.text: Sensible? Lear could not be so described

definitions.text: Lear could not be so described

explanation.surface: Wonders whether Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, could be called sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear was famous for nonsense verse, so his writing was anything but free of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone practical and down-to-earth is called no-nonsense.

clue.text: Incomer could be upset by a trimming

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of the following words being knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A newcomer might be offended by having their hair trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is someone who comes into a country to settle: an incomer.

clue.text: Charming, but to some extent self-indulgent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the following word is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Someone is charming, but a little self-indulgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes a delicate, small and appealing charm, like that of an elf.

clue.text: Lady shopping may be, in a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A woman out shopping is, one might say, doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: A shopper chasing the latest style is literally pursuing a fashion; the phrase also means 'loosely, in a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in some sense or to a certain extent, just as 'in a manner of speaking' does.

clue.text: Plaited fibres in its sole are spilled out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are spilled out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes rope-soled shoes, whose plaited fibres spill out.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe whose sole is made of plaited rope or esparto fibre.

clue.text: Astronauts' pub used by typists?

explanation.surface: Wonders whether typists drink in a bar for astronauts.
explanation.walkthrough: A bar in space would be a space bar; the long key on a keyboard has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the long key a typist presses to put gaps between words.

clue.text: Mysterious exit opened, letting out nothing suitable

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the letters are jumbled into something new
letting out means one letter is released from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: O is nothing, the figure zero

explanation.surface: A strange exit is opened, but nothing is let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from EXITOPENED and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient or suitable for a purpose.

clue.text: Decorative band of cloth

explanation.surface: A strip of ornamental fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the ornamental strip along a wall; the other is a coarse woollen cloth with a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecturally the word names a decorated horizontal strip; in textiles, a heavy napped woollen fabric.

clue.text: Did former wife finally have pretty daughter ?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of wife

parts.note: cute means pretty

explanation.surface: Asks whether a former wife eventually had a pretty daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Executed means carried out or performed, just as 'did' does.

clue.text: Short bar put in different position

indicators.note: putting letters in a different position means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A short bar is placed somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt reply is a short, curt one.

clue.text: Use less accurate figure — 0, and higher

parts.note: the figure zero is round in shape, a round
up means higher

explanation.surface: Advice to approximate a number, zero, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up is to replace an exact number with a less precise, larger one.

clue.text: Fanatics go to these ends

parts.note: zealots are said to go to great lengths, pushing things to their furthest limits, and 'ends' is a synonym for those limits

explanation.surface: Describes the lengths zealots will go to.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremes are the furthest ends of a range, the places fanatics are proverbially driven to.

clue.text: Pretend to understand

explanation.surface: To feign comprehension.
explanation.walkthrough: To make out is to claim or pretend ('he made out he was ill') and also to discern or understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Making out can mean claiming falsely or managing to understand something.

clue.text: Carpenter's fast food outlet

explanation.surface: A carpenter's takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Chippy is British slang for a carpenter and for a fish-and-chip shop; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for a joiner, who makes chips of wood, and a fish-and-chip shop.

clue.text: What some golfers play all day long

explanation.surface: Some golfers play from dawn till dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names a practice game played at holes or targets set out like a clock face, and also means continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means through all twenty-four hours, continuously; it is also a game of shots from twelve positions.

clue.text: Statuette awarded by very big wheels

parts.note: OS means outsize, very big
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A trophy handed out by Hollywood bigwigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big wheels' suggests important people; it splits as 'very big' plus 'wheels'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the gold statuette awarded by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

clue.text: White has a go

parts.note: a shy is a go or throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone named White takes a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means pale or ash-coloured, a deathly whitish grey.

clue.text: Deposit obsolete coin in box

indicators.note: in tells us the coin goes inside the box

parts.note: a loge is a box in a theatre
D stood for the old British penny, the pre-1971 coin

explanation.surface: Someone puts an old coin away in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence, with d the symbol for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge something, such as a complaint or valuables, is to deposit it.

clue.text: Voters have to communicate comprehensibly

explanation.surface: Voters must explain themselves clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British ballot paper a voter marks a cross by the chosen name.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea over clearly to an audience is to put it across.

clue.text: The ultimate way to disrupt my identification

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last one
to disrupt the word my, another word breaks into the middle of it

parts.note: a path is a way

explanation.surface: The final method of throwing off someone's identification of me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' gives E from The; 'to disrupt' puts PATH between the M and Y of my.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is identification with another person's feelings.

clue.text: Woman's books husband concealed in boat

indicators.note: concealed in means hidden inside the next word's letters

parts.note: a dory is a small flat-bottomed boat
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A woman's reading matter and her husband are tucked away in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy is a woman's name.
